summary: The round-1 findings are fixed. F1: return paths now allow only URL-safe ASCII, and the listener catches a rejected gateway request; a temp test sends %01, %7F, %E2%82%AC and an encoded CRLF and then checks /health. F2: on HTTPS, the setup browser cookie is `__Host-halo_setup_<id>` and only that name is read. F3: the stack is rebased, and both test runs pass. One gap remains: the new error backstop in the creator-host request listener is neither covered nor exempt, so the coverage gate fails.

findings.body: The new backstop for a rejected `appGateway.serve()` (lines 188 and 191-193: wrap the error, log it, answer 500, end the response) is uncovered and has no exemption, so the coverage gate fails. Either add a temp test that makes `serve()` reject and checks that the visitor gets 500 and that `/health` still answers, or mark these lines `coverage-exempt` with a concrete reason. One way to make `serve()` reject: give the appWorld provider fixture a `getConnection` that throws instead of returning an error. An acceptable reason is that this is a defensive backstop and no known input still throws inside `AppGateway.serve`.

testRequests.target: apps/control-plane/src/server/controlPlaneHttp.ts:184-195: a creator-host request whose AppGateway.serve rejects
testRequests.rationale: Shows that the backstop answers 500 instead of crashing the process. Without it, lines 188 and 191-193 stay uncovered; the other option is a justified coverage-exempt mark.
